- NVIDIA reports Data Center revenue as a market-platform figure in its earnings-release segment tables, not as a line item of the primary financial statements. [1][2]
- Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended April 27, 2025) Data Center revenue was $39,112 million, up 10% sequentially as disclosed. [1]
- Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended July 27, 2025) Data Center revenue was $41,096 million, up 5% sequentially as disclosed. [2]
- Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended October 26, 2025) Data Center revenue was $51,215 million, up 25% sequentially as disclosed. [3]
- Q4 FY2026 (quarter ended January 25, 2026) Data Center revenue was $62,314 million, up 22% sequentially as disclosed. [4]
- Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended April 26, 2026) Data Center revenue was $75,246 million, up 21% sequentially as disclosed. [5]
- Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 26, 2026) Data Center revenue was $89,023 million, up 18% sequentially as disclosed. [6]
- Beginning in Q1 FY2027 NVIDIA changed its reporting framework to two market platforms, Data Center and Edge Computing, with Data Center split into Hyperscale and ACIE sub-markets. [7][5]
